newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to review banks with foreign T-bill rights.
newsitem.headline: Russia to review banks with foreign T-bill rights.

text.p: Russia's central bank plans to review at the end of September the list of banks that have the right to open special "S" rouble accounts for foreigners trading T-bills, a senior bank official has said.
Central bank first deputy chairman Andrei Kozlov told Reuters only five of the 22 Russian and foreign banks on the list were active, and some of the others may be replaced.
"We will assess the success of the Russian banks and consider either increasing the number able to work with S accounts or replacing somebody," Kozlov said.
The list includes 21 Russian banks and Swiss bank Credit Suisse, which was recently added to the list.
"Among those who have received licences, some have not begun to operate, and that is rather disappointing," he said.
He said a further 10 or so banks, including regional ones, wanted permission to work with S accounts but that there were no immediate plans to increase the list.

Foreigners have since August 15 been able to open the special rouble accounts and use funds in them to trade in the government securities market, buy and sell at auction and trade in the secondary market.

The aim was to attract foreign investment into the government securities market to bring down yields. But foreign investment so far has been disappointingly low because the scheme has been poorly marketed, bankers said.
